content.value_statement: Kotlin asynchronous code can fail through leaks, missed cancellation, and unclear Flow behavior. This skill guides structured concurrency, Flow design, error handling, and coroutine testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use coroutineScope and supervisorScope for grouped asynchronous work.
Shows how to handle coroutine errors with try-catch and CoroutineExceptionHandler.
Compares cold Flow, StateFlow, and SharedFlow for stream and state design.
Demonstrates parallel coroutine work with async, await, and supervisorScope.
Gives testing guidance with TestScope, runTest, and TestDispatcher.
limitations: Does not run Kotlin code or verify compiler errors by itself.
Does not include full Android architecture guidance beyond coroutine usage.
Does not cover every Flow operator or advanced backpressure pattern.
Requires users to provide project context for precise implementation advice.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Coroutine Tests

prompt_templates.title: Explain Coroutine Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of core coroutine concepts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how structured concurrency should guide my Kotlin coroutine design. Use simple examples and mention common mistakes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Flow State Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design review for streams and UI state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Kotlin Flow design for search, UI state, and one-time events. Recommend where to use Flow, StateFlow, or SharedFlow.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Cancellation And Errors
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced troubleshooting for production coroutine behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help debug coroutine cancellation and error propagation in this feature. Identify scope problems, swallowed exceptions, and retry risks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Coroutine Test Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced testing plan for asynchronous Kotlin code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a coroutine testing strategy for suspending functions and Flows. Include dispatcher injection, virtual time, and failure scenarios.

output_examples.input: A developer asks why parallel dashboard loading cancels all work when one request fails.
output_examples.output: The skill explains the difference between coroutineScope and supervisorScope, then recommends isolating optional requests from required data.

output_examples.input: An Android team asks whether a screen event should use StateFlow or SharedFlow.
output_examples.output: The skill compares retained state with transient events, then recommends StateFlow for UI state and SharedFlow for one-time events.

output_examples.input: A test suite hangs while testing delayed Flow emissions.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends runTest, injected test dispatchers, and virtual time control to make coroutine tests deterministic.

best_practices: Prefer structured scopes that match the lifetime of the work.
Rethrow CancellationException when handling broad coroutine failures.
Inject dispatchers so production code and tests can use different execution contexts.
anti_patterns: Do not use GlobalScope for routine application work.
Do not hide coroutine failures behind broad catches without logging or recovery.
Do not test coroutines with real delays when virtual time is available.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design, debug, and test Kotlin Coroutines and Flow patterns.

faq.question: Can it write complete Kotlin features?
faq.answer: It can guide feature structure and examples, but users should compile and test the final code.

faq.question: Does it cover Android ViewModel usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses viewModelScope, retained UI state, and lifecycle-aware coroutine patterns.

faq.question: Does it explain Flow operators?
faq.answer: It covers common operators such as debounce, flatMapLatest, and flowOn in practical scenarios.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky coroutine tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends runTest, TestScope, TestDispatcher, and virtual time control.

faq.answer: The reviewed file is documentation only and contains no command execution behavior.
